themes_detail.label: Panhandling surge this week
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints spiked to 7 this week versus a baseline average of 1.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 331% increase—suggesting a sudden influx or visibility shift in the district that warrants street-level reporting.
evidence: 7 panhandling complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (331% spike, z-score: 4.08)
Statistically significant anomaly (z-score 4.08, severity marked high)
Most recent spike data point in dataset, indicating emerging pattern
reporting_angles: Door-knock interviews with residents and business owners on Myrtle, DeKalb, and Flatbush avenues to understand if panhandling has visibly increased or if complaints reflect new enforcement
Interview NYPD and local precinct about whether they've noticed uptick in panhandling and what outreach/services are available

themes_detail.label: Street light outages spike
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints jumped to 22 this week from a baseline average of 9.1 weekly over the prior 8 weeks—a 141% increase—pointing to potential infrastructure failures in lighting that could affect public safety perception and evening street activity.
evidence: 22 street light complaints THIS WEEK vs. 9.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (141% spike, z-score: 4.0)
High z-score (4.0) indicates statistically significant departure from baseline
Aligns with recurring CB budget requests for DOT infrastructure upgrades, suggesting chronic underfunding
reporting_angles: Map the 22 complaints geographically to identify dark corridors (parks, residential blocks, transit hubs) and photograph affected areas
Request DOE maintenance records to determine if recent budget cuts or staffing changes have delayed repairs; ask CB about backlog of infrastructure requests

themes_detail.label: Door/window security complaints up 96%
themes_detail.summary: Door and window-related complaints (likely break-ins, security concerns) reached 13 this week versus a baseline of 6.6 per week over 8 weeks—a 96% increase—indicating a possible property crime cluster that needs ground-truthing.
evidence: 13 door/window complaints THIS WEEK vs. 6.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (96% spike, z-score: 4.84)
High severity flagged in data; z-score of 4.84 is highly anomalous
Timing suggests potential recent crime wave or seasonal shift in burglary activity
reporting_angles: Cross-reference with NYPD crime data (burglary, petit larceny) for same week to verify if 311 complaints track actual crime reports
Interview residents in clusters where complaints are concentrated; speak to local precinct about enforcement response and prevention recommendations

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary conditions nearly doubled
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints surged to 33 last week from a baseline of 16.6 per week over 8 weeks—a 98% increase—indicating a potential sanitation crisis (overflowing trash, rodent signs, or illegal dumping) concentrated in specific blocks or venues.
evidence: 33 unsanitary condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 16.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (98% spike, z-score: 3.57)
High severity and z-score above 3.5 indicate sustained anomaly
Aligns with long-term CB budget requests for DEP (sanitation) expense support
reporting_angles: Visit top complaint blocks to photograph and document sanitation failures; identify whether trash collection has been delayed or if new construction/demolition is creating debris
Interview Sanitation Department about pickup schedules and staffing; ask CB about funding requests for expanded service in high-density areas like Brooklyn Heights waterfront

themes_detail.label: Park noise complaints skyrocketing
themes_detail.summary: Noise in parks spiked to 5 complaints two weeks ago from a baseline average of just 0.1 per week—a 3900% increase, the most extreme anomaly in the dataset—suggesting a specific event, construction, or new venue activity disrupting outdoor spaces.
evidence: 5 park noise complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3900% spike, z-score: 14.74, highest severity)
Extraordinary z-score (14.74) indicates this is the most statistically anomalous complaint type in the district
However, absolute volume is low (only 5 complaints), so requires ground verification of cause
reporting_angles: Identify which parks (Fort Greene, Brooklyn Bridge, St. Felix) generated the 5 complaints; cross-check with Parks Dept event calendar for concerts, festivals, or construction
Interview Parks Dept and CB Parks Committee about whether a temporary event or new permitted activity (outdoor dining, performance venue) is driving noise; assess if pattern sustained or one-off
